text:
linda_sales: Quick post from the Acme POC today. We ran a mixed surge test they asked for. High level: sustained 180 qps baseline with 20 qps 30s microbursts to 400 qps. Observed embedding queueing + long-gen timeouts. Need: 1) short pricing delta (hosted vs reserved burst), 2) security questionnaire answers + KMS note, 3) ops check on why autoscale lagged.

ashwin_se: can you share the exact load profile and the command? curious if embedding batching was on and whether responses used KV cache for chat.

linda_sales: load command we kicked off with loadbot: 

```
runbot simulate --target https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  --profile "baseline:180,burst:400:30s@300s" --duration 600s \
  --mix chat=0.6,emb=0.3,long=0.1 --model redwood/gptx-7b:quant-v2 --region us-east-1
```

runbot: finished run_id=acme-surge-2026-04-02. Summary: avg_latency=135ms, p95=260ms, p99=1700ms, max=4100ms, 1.1% errors (mostly long-gen timeouts). Embedding requests had a steady CPU-bound tail when not batched. KV cache enabled for chat.

troy_ops: saw the logs briefly. autoscaler started scale-up at t+45s but GPUs were provisioned at t+140s due to cold slot allocation in the dedicated pool. Burst window too short for autoscale to be effective. Also noticed embedding worker threads were pinned on CPU on the inference proxy; batching disabled in the test.

maria_prod: product ask: customer wants predictable p95 < 300ms for mixed workload and p99 < 1s for short chat. They also asked about CMK with HSM and SSO integration notes.

linda_sales: ok. Sales action: draft quick delta so they have numbers today. I sketched a rough calc: 
  - Hosted estimate: token cost ~ $0.0008/token (gen) and embedding unit ~$0.0015/embed req; for this workload monthly ~ $8k.
  - Reserved burst (small dedicated pool): monthly commit ~ $3.5k + reduced per-token ~ $6k effective -> combined ~ $9.5k but much lower tail latency.
  - Note: numbers are illustrative, need infra confirmation.

ashwin_se: mitigation notes for next run: 1) enable adaptive embedding batching (batch window 25ms), 2) widen burst_window to 180s, 3) warm dedicated nodes before burst using pre-warm API, 4) increase per-request timeout for long-gen to 12s so we reduce errors. Config snippet below: 

```json
{
  "adaptive_batching": true,
  "embedding_batch_ms": 25,
  "burst_window_secs": 180,
  "prewarm_nodes": 2,
  "request_timeout_secs": 12
}
```

troy_ops: I'll pull autoscale events and deployment timings and post the log snippet. If prewarm is used, latency for cold allocation should drop < 60s. Also recommend a tiny reserved pool (2 vGPU nodes) for long-gen stability.

maria_prod: for security: they want KMS CMK HSM-backed. We support bringing your own CMK via our KMS bridging; note their compliance team also asked for a diagram of the encryption flow and a signed ALA. I'll attach the questionnaire answers tomorrow.

linda_sales: great. Action items: 
  - ashwin_se: update runbook + PR with the config snippet and recommended flags.
  - troy_ops: post autoscale logs and confirm prewarm behavior.
  - sales: I'll produce a tightened pricing delta and note reserved sizing assumptions (2-node pool, expected concurrency per node). Aim EOD.
  - maria_prod: complete security answers + KMS flow diagram by EOD tomorrow.

runbot: marker: run_id=acme-surge-2026-04-02 results_uploaded link=https://internal.storage/acme-surge-2026-04-02.json

linda_sales: thanks team. Planning a follow-up call with Acme on Monday to discuss reserved pool tradeoffs vs hosted. Will post the pricing draft here when ready. :thumbsup:
